statement: AWS published EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML per-accelerator-hour rates effective October 7, 2026, with P6-B300 at $16.146 per accelerator-hour and no prior rates shown for comparison.
why: This is a static rental price level with no stated baseline or change, so it serves as a display overlay on GPU rental pricing rather than a directional signal.

impact.mechanism: Published reserved-block accelerator rental rates set the visible cost of renting NVIDIA accelerators from a hyperscaler, which anchors buy-versus-rent comparisons without itself indicating a change.

evidence.excerpt: the page publishes no prior rates. No direction of change -- up, down, or flat -- can be established from what AWS has published.

confidence.basis: Single secondary outlet restating a vendor pricing page; the article itself states no prior rates are published, and the circulating 15% increase framing traces to an unconfirmed social post.

dispersion: Per accelerator-hour: P6-B300 $16.146, P6-B200 $14.208, P5en $7.895, P5e $6.866, P5 $5.970, P4de $2.546, P4d $1.696; GovCloud about 4.17% higher for P6.
